A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAVL benchmark and SylAVL-CoT research. All pages, including Appendices A–I, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original translation experiments, ablations, dataset analyses, and a user study in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons, user study, and appendix cross-lingual evaluations.

M1.justification: The syllable segmentation, video-informed translation, and iterative refinement procedure in Section 3.2 and Appendix F is unchanged. Replacing 'Ours' with 'Gemini 2.0' identifies the existing implementation; Gemini 2.5 experiments already appear in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MAVL collection of 228 songs across five languages, with identical dataset statistics. English-source evaluations and the additional language-pair coverage in Appendix C.4 are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments. The rows renamed from 'Gemini' to 'Gemini 2.0' retain their results and correspond to the Gemini 2.0 Flash baseline already identified in v3 Section 4.1.

E3.justification: Metrics, reference comparisons, modality controls, generation settings, and user-study design are unchanged. Adding '(w/ SC)' to the upper Gemini rows in Tables 12–13 clarifies conditions already indicated by the corresponding dubbed-reference rows and Table 14 in v3.

E4.justification: The modality ablations, syllable-list/refinement ablations, cross-model CoT analysis, dataset similarity analysis, and qualitative examples are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Table 9 retains mean scores with standard deviations and N = 10 participants per language. Neither the statistical reporting practices nor the reported run/seed information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains English-reference Spanish syllable errors of 0.966 for Gemini 2.0 SylAVL-CoT and 0.918 for its Gemini 2.5 variant.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and equations in Section 3.3, including the syllable penalty, remain unchanged, as does Appendix A. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, SylAVL-CoT contribution, and claims about singability and contextual accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality effects, paraphrasing, model evolution, and cross-lingual performance are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning data scope, line-level translation, tonal languages, alignment, metrics, and broader applicability.

D1.justification: Dataset reconstruction, alignment instructions, prompts, preprocessing libraries, computational resources, generation configurations, and code/data access information are unchanged. The clearer table labels repeat model identities and conditions already documented in v3.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The final references move onto an additional page, but no scholarly references are added or removed.

P1.justification: v5 adds funding acknowledgements, updates the corresponding author's email, and standardizes model labels. The scientific prose and ordering of the main sections and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing tables receive clearer model/condition labels, with some resizing and surrounding text reflow. Figures 1–9 and the table organization are retained; the acknowledgements and reflow leave the final two references on an additional page.

improvement.justification: Explicit Gemini 2.0 labels and consistent syllable-constraint labels make the existing comparisons easier to interpret without cross-referencing other passages. Funding acknowledgements also improve transparency. These are limited presentation gains; the methods, empirical support, and scientific limitations remain unchanged.
